headline: Methods link GWAS loci, gene-environment effects, and epistasis to biological mechanism
label: Genetic Association Inference Methods
summary: Recent 2026 studies extend association analysis beyond single-locus effects toward tissue context, environmental interaction, and epistatic architecture.
synthesis: The dominant thread is moving association inference beyond marginal locus-level effects toward mechanistic and interaction-aware models. J-PEP partitions GWAS loci by combining pleiotropic SNP effects with tissue epigenomic data, reporting 16%-30% higher PEPA across 165 traits. A cross-population gene-environment interaction compendium spans 440k European and Japanese individuals with replication in 540k, linking interactions to polygenic prediction and lipid genetics. EpiDetect introduces EpiCID, an explainability algorithm for neural networks, to infer SNP epistatic interaction networks from blood pressure GWAS data. Together these studies address context dependence in genetic effects: tissue, environment, and genetic background. The new elements are the integration of epigenomic annotation into locus partitioning, large-scale replicated interaction mapping across ancestries, and interpretable deep learning for epistasis.
